title: Applications of invariant subspaces: diagonalizability criteria and simultaneous triangulation
objectives: Prove that an operator is triangulable exactly when its minimal polynomial splits
Prove the distinct-linear-factor criterion for diagonalizability
Construct triangularizing bases and test the criteria on examples
Triangularize a commuting family with one basis
prerequisites: Invariant subspaces and conductors (Chapter 15), the minimal polynomial and eigenvalues (Chapters 12 to 14).
source_scope: The captions of the two recordings (positions 32 and 33) were read in full. The running matrix and the integral-operator example come from them; the commuting-family section, the extended proofs, the laboratory and the exercises are additions.
